subject: Cooking
title: Wooden Cutting Boards Are Less Hygienic — Myth
description: A micro-lesson that makes Wooden Cutting Boards Are Less Hygienic — Myth usable.

hook.text: Health codes once banned wooden boards. Research proved they're actually safer than plastic.

buildup.text: Plastic boards seem easier to clean — smooth, non-porous, and dishwasher-safe.

discovery.text: UC Davis research found bacteria sink into wood grain and die. On scarred plastic, bacteria thrive in grooves.

twist.text: New plastic boards are fine. But after knife scarring, plastic harbors more bacteria than well-maintained wood.

climax.text: Many health departments have reversed their bans — wood is now accepted in professional kitchens again.

punchline.text: The 'dirty' wooden board was cleaner all along.

quiz.question: What happens to bacteria on wooden cutting boards?
options: They sink into the grain and die

details.summary: Wood cutting boards are not less hygienic than plastic — in fact research suggests the opposite. Wood has natural antimicrobial properties, and bacteria drawn into wood grain die rather than multiply. Plastic boards develop knife scars that harbor bacteria and are harder to sanitize.
details.whyItMatters: Decades of advice to avoid wooden boards was based on assumption, not evidence. Understanding that wood has natural antimicrobial properties reverses this long-held kitchen misconception.
takeaways: Wood's natural properties draw in and kill bacteria below the surface
Scarred plastic boards harbor more bacteria than wood boards
Both materials are safe when properly cleaned and maintained

faq.question: What does the research actually show?
faq.answer: UC Davis microbiologist Dean Cliver found that bacteria placed on wooden boards were killed by the wood's antimicrobial properties. On plastic boards, bacteria survived in knife scars even after washing. New plastic boards and well-maintained wood boards both test clean after proper washing.

faq.question: How should you care for wooden cutting boards?
faq.answer: Wash with hot soapy water after each use. Do not soak or put in the dishwasher since this warps and cracks wood. Sanitize periodically with diluted white vinegar. Oil with food-grade mineral oil monthly to maintain the surface. Replace when deep cracks develop.
